title: Convoy HI-67, 29 June 1944
eyebrow: Marianas lifeguard and Luzon Strait · BANG's second war patrol, in a pack with SEAHORSE and GROWLER

paras.text: BANG's attack on convoy HI-67, bound from Moji for Singapore by way of Manila, as typed on her attack sheets, beside the escort division's chart of the same afternoon.

Oilers Miri Maru and Sarawak Maru were hit, minor damage, and both reached Manila; neither is in the June list of ships sunk by submarine. BANG claimed two ships sunk and one probably sunk. Her sheet 2(b)'s "large hole under bridge" matches Miri Maru, hit under the bridge. The night before, 28 June, GROWLER sank a large tanker and an escort from a different convoy 130 nm to the northeast (her claim), then left for home on fuel.

Moji to Singapore by way of Manila. The escort division's chart names only the two ships hit; FRUPAC's map gives the convoy as 1 CVS, 5 escorts and 10 AK/AP. The convoy's own record: [[convoy:hi-67]].

Positions are BANG's own dead reckoning and star sights; lines between them are straight, and where she went in between is not recorded. Open circles are ships she sighted, at the target's position. As the clock passes each firing time a red ring pulses at BANG's position; hover a diamond for the attack sheet.

BANG kept zone K (−10) for Attack 1 and zone I (−9) for Attacks 2 and 3, as her report does; GROWLER kept I on station, but SEAHORSE kept H (−8). Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9): the escort division's chart has HI-67's two oilers hit at 1515, seven minutes after BANG's sheet.

No Japanese record has been found yet for Attacks 1 and 3; those actions show only the American side. Where the Japanese record names only the ships that were hit, the rest of the convoy is described as the boats saw it.

BANG's second war patrol report, NARA microfilm M1752 (74802784); SEAHORSE Patrol 5 (74845019); GROWLER Patrol 9 (74818866). The 1st Surface Escort Division war diary, June 1944, via JACAR (C08030141000, National Institute for Defense Studies). Sarawak Maru's record from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

fixes.fix: ship-contact positions are the target, not BANG

outcome.note: Oilers Miri Maru and Sarawak Maru of HI-67 (Moji to Singapore via Manila), both minor damage; both reached Manila. BANG's sheets claimed 2(a) a large engine-aft freighter or tanker sunk (fits Sarawak Maru, hit in the bow), 2(b) a large passenger freighter sunk with a hole under the bridge (fits Miri Maru, hit under the bridge), and 2(c) a freighter probably sunk (no Japanese record of a third ship hit). FRUPAC relayed the claim as 2 AK sunk, 1 AK probably sunk

events.title: Ordered 450 ft
events.words: saw second MARU in east column firing what looked like 20 m.m. tracers at us ... range 600 yards so ordered 450 feet.

events.title: Sarawak Maru and Miri Maru
events.words: BANG fires all ten tubes at three ships at about 1510; Sarawak Maru is hit in the bow and Miri Maru under the bridge, and both reach Manila
events.note: Secondary source (combinedfleet.com). Secondary. Time "about 1510" is BANG's (sheet 1508-1509 I); position is the source's. Temporary repairs at Cavite until 24 July

events.title: Passing 200 ft (1)
events.words: The first depth charge close but above us as we passed 200 feet

events.title: Ordered 500 ft (125)
events.words: A sustained depth charge attack totalling 125 charges started six minutes after the attack. Ran at standard speed for ten minutes then evaded on steady course at 2/3 speed at 500 feet. We were under a 16° negative temperature gradient.

events.title: Miri Maru and Sarawak Maru
events.words: 29th, 1515, N 17°13′ E 118°22′: Miri Maru and Sarawak Maru (minor damage)
events.original: 二九日 一五一五 N一七-一三 E一一八-二二 みりい丸 さらわく丸 (小破)

events.title: Ordered 400 ft
events.words: After reloading at 400 feet with no depth charges for an hour and a half

events.title: Depth charges (17)
events.words: Saw two CHIDORI torpedo boats ... range 14000 yards. They dropped 17 depth charges at 1937

paras.text: Moji to Singapore by way of Manila, June–July 1944. The escort division's June chart starts the track in the 22 June column (Kurahashi joined from Sasebo that day: combinedfleet:Kurahashi_t, secondary); the sailing date of 20 June is combinedfleet.com's (secondary). The July chart has the convoy leave Manila on the 3rd with 7 ships and reach 昭南 on the 9th.

**Cargo: not recorded** in any record read. The southbound HI convoys took oilers to Singapore to load (inferred, not from a record of this convoy). Miri Maru's designated-ship log (jacar:C08050103600 p21–25) ends on 10 June 1944, when the Navy took her over, so it stops before this voyage. Gokoku, Asahisan, Miri and Sarawak Maru left the convoy at Manila (combinedfleet, secondary).

words.type_attack: Day periscope attack. Fired four torpedoes using 2° spread between torpedoes, applied from aft forward by means of the offset knob on the TDC. Kept continuous periscope bearings to the TDC during firing.
words.description: Large engine aft MARU. Considerable superstructure amidships, believed to be freighter, but possibly a tanker. One of convoy of at least 11 MARUS including two tankers and one possible C.S, with five or more escorts, two of which were identified as CHIDORI torpedo boats. Contact initially made by sighting smoke in dawn twilight. Visibility unlimited at time of attack. Estimate uncertain.
words.sunk: One large engine aft freighter or tanker.
words.determined_by: Heard three hits in this MARU. Saw large hole amidships that had blown up through the deck. Heard loud explosion followed by heavy persistent rumbling noise three minutes after she was hit.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 29' Course: 225° Speed: 14.0 Range: 1750 yds.
words.note: The Hit or Miss row is typed "3 Hits" across the four columns, not per torpedo, so attacks.csv's `hit` is blank for tubes 1-4. Tube 4's Mark 14-3A is circled by hand on the scan.

words.type_attack: Day periscope attack. This ship selected as primary target of convoy - TDC kept set up on her and one sound head trained constantly on her with bearings coming in continuously until just before firing, when set-up was shifted to target at greater range (attack No. 2(a)), then back to her. Fired two torpedoes spread 2° aft and 2° forward of MOT with offset knob on TDC. Kept continuous periscope bearings to TDC during firing.
words.description: Large passenger freighter of convoy of attack No. 2(a). This ship was selected early in the approach as the best target of the group with the exception of a possible CVS astern of her. She was very long with two goal posts forward and two aft. Estimate uncertain.
words.determined_by: Heard two hits in this MARU. Saw large hole under bridge that had blown up through deck and blown port half of bridge away. Target listed 20° to port, deck line under and going down.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 29' Course: 225° Speed: 14.0 Range: 750 yds.
words.note: Typed at 1508 (I), the same minute as 2(a); 2(c)'s remarks put 17 seconds between 2(a) and 2(b). Its sheet starts at p27, not the p25 positions.csv cites for Attack 2. The Mark 14-3A entries are circled by hand.

words.type_attack: Day periscope attack with stern tubes immediately after firing bow tubes in attacks 2(a) and 2(b). Torpedoes spread 1° aft, 0°, 0°, and 1° forward by means of the offset knob on the TDC. Target observed to be turning slowly away during firing. Angle on the bow 20° less than that estimated was given to TDC to give less lead angle to torpedoes and thus allow for turn during torpedo run.
words.description: Freighter similar to TERUKAWA MARU, page 198, ONI 208-J (revised). This ship was not smoking at all at 14 knots. One of convoy of attack No. 2(a). Estimate certain.
words.probably_sunk: One freighter similar to TERUKAWA MARU.
words.determined_by: Heard three torpex hits in this MARU timed and spaced perfectly for torpedoes fired at her.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 26' Course: 205° Speed: 14.0 Range: 1300 yds.
words.remarks: On attacks 2(a) and 2(c) a point of aim 1/4 of target length inside stern was taken since the range to the target was sufficient to allow for maneuver to avoid on sighting the wakes, and with angle on the bow near 90° any appreciable maneuver in either direction would tend to make the torpedoes pass ahead. On attack 2(c), since target was actually observed to be turning away, the angle on the bow was deliberately underestimated by 20° as a further precaution against the torpedoes passing ahead. On attack 2(b) the target was so close that no maneuver could cause the torpedoes to miss, so the MOT was taken as point of aim. The 17 seconds between attack 2(a) and 2(b) seemed long, and the 51 seconds between 2(b) and 2(c) was like as many minutes. In my anxiety to get the stern torpedoes out as soon as possible I said something that influenced the officer at the firing key to fire No. 7 tube before a solution was generated. I also told the assistant TDC operator to use 2° spread for the stern tubes, meaning 2° between torpedoes. This was my mistake since the approach party has been instructed that I will always give over-all spread. A stern tube spread of 1L, 0, 0, 1R was set, whereas 3L, 1L, 1R, 3R was intended. Fortunately the spread coverage was not needed. Steps have been taken to prevent a recurrence of the above mistake.
words.note: Typed at 1509 (I); positions.csv's Attack 2 is 1508 (2(a)'s time). The sheet starts at p29, not the p25 positions.csv cites. Tube 7 has its track typed "*" and gyro "060*" (the footnote: solution not generated), kept as typed. Tubes 8-10's typed tracks (105S, 108S, 111S) are each about 4° wider than own course 320 + gyro + 180 - the typed target course 205 gives (101S, 103.5S, 107S): kept as typed; the remarks say the angle on the bow given to the TDC was 20° less than estimated, so the TDC's target course was not the 205 typed here.
